title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. In it Grothendieck describes crystals on a smooth S over a perfect field k as coherent modules with stratification, or equivalently with an integrable connection, on a formal lift X of S over R = Spf W(k). Isocrystals are described as stratified coherent modules on the rigid generic fibre X_K.

The paragraph that starts on the previous page (§1.14) explains how to make the Frobenius pullback M ↦ M^(p) explicit in this description. That is the step needed to define bicrystals (F, V).

General principle: given a commutative square S' → S over Spec k' → Spec k, with compatible formal lifts X' → X over Spf W' → Spf W, pullback of crystals becomes ordinary pullback of stratified modules from X to X'.

Specialisation to Frobenius (k = k', S = S', the maps being p-th powers): one needs a lift f_X : X → X of the absolute Frobenius f_S that is compatible with the Witt-vector Frobenius f_W on Spf W. Equivalently, one lifts the relative Frobenius S → S^(p/k) to an R-morphism X → X ×_{R,f_R} R. Such a lift always exists when S is affine; then X is formally smooth and affine, so lifts exist step by step, and one may reduce to this case.

With such an f_X:
- the functor M ↦ M^(p) is ordinary pullback of stratified O_X-modules along f_X;
- for isocrystals it is pullback along the f_K-semilinear rigid morphism X_K → X_K;
- although f_X is far from unique, the resulting functor does not depend on the choice, up to canonical isomorphism. The reason is that the stratification (Taylor isomorphism) identifies the pullbacks along any two lifts.

§1.15 drops the assumption of a fixed characteristic. For a scheme S over Z and each prime p, let S_p = V(p·1) be the fibre over p. A bicrystal of weight i on S is a crystal of modules M on S together with, for every p, a weight-i bicrystal structure (F_p, V_p with F_p V_p = p^i) on the restriction M_p to S_p. Bi-isocrystals are defined the same way, where isocrystals are obtained from crystals by tensoring Hom groups with Q.
- In characteristic 0 the extra structure is empty.
- In characteristic p one recovers §1.10.
- For S of finite type and dominant over Spec Z the notion is 'arithmetic': the F_p play the role of Frobenius at each prime.
- In weight 1 (continued on the next page), the bicrystal is meant to link the formal groups in the various characteristics arising from one global object, for example H^1_dR of an abelian scheme with its Gauss–Manin connection and Frobenius/Verschiebung at every p.
errors: No substantive error. Existence of a Frobenius lift is asserted only in the affine case, and the reduction to that case implicitly needs gluing (the 'champ' condition), which the next page admits was handled carelessly.
Independence of choice of f_X is asserted without proof. It holds via the Taylor isomorphism / stratification, giving canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along different lifts.

For isocrystals the rigid description implicitly assumes the full-faithfulness and essential-image issues raised on the previous page. The rigid pullback is fine, but the essential image (convergent connections) is not addressed.

ideas.what: Making the Frobenius pullback of crystals explicit via a lift of Frobenius to a formal lift X, and independence of the choice of lift
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius structure on crystals via local Frobenius lifts; F-crystals / Dieudonné crystals in terms of modules with connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Tate, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' 1968), Berthelot (1974), Berthelot–Ogus (1978), Katz
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), notes by Coleman; ideas of the Tate letter

ideas.what: Frobenius pullback of isocrystals as pullback of stratified modules along a semilinear rigid-analytic Frobenius X_K → X_K
ideas.where_published: Tate letter (circulated); not in the 1968 Dix exposés text as far as I know

ideas.what: Bicrystals / bi-isocrystals over an arbitrary base S over Z: a crystal on S plus (F_p, V_p) on each fibre S_p
ideas.modern_name: Global object with F-crystal structure at every prime (cf. de Rham cohomology with Gauss–Manin connection plus crystalline Frobenius at all p; 'compatible systems' of F-crystals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard single attribution; related ideas in Honda's theory of formal groups over Z (1968–70), Fontaine–Messing, Faltings, Borger's Λ-geometry
ideas.where_published: Tate letter (1966) only, as far as I know

missed.claim: In weight 1 over a base dominating Spec Z, Grothendieck proposes the 'bicrystal' (crystal plus F_p, V_p at all primes) as the device linking the formal groups in different characteristics coming from one global object. This anticipates Honda's 1968–70 theory, which classifies formal groups over Z and Z_p by Frobenius-type data at each prime (the 'type' of the logarithm, Hazewinkel's functional-equation lemma). The literature does not seem to link Honda's theory to this crystalline 'bi-structure at all primes' proposal.
missed.quote: Lorsque enfin S est de type fini sur Z et domine Spec(Z), alors la notion envisagée est d'une nature essentiellement arithmétique, les différents F_p jouant le rôle d'homomorphismes de frobenius
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A global category of crystals with Frobenius at every prime is close to current interests: Λ-structures and Borger's 'F_1' geometry, global prismatic or Witt-vector cohomology, and integral p-adic Hodge theory done uniformly in p. Grothendieck's early formulation is a natural historical antecedent rarely cited.

missed.claim: The definition of bicrystals over an arbitrary base is only sketched. It is left open what the right category is, which functors (e.g. from abelian schemes or p-divisible data) it receives, and whether it classifies anything, for instance formal groups over Z.
missed.quote: Un bicristal de poids i sur S est par définition la donnée d'un cristal de modules M sur S, et pour chaque p d'une structure de bi-cristal de poids i sur la restriction M_p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such a global 'all-primes' Dieudonné-type theory over Z was never systematised in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The Frobenius-lift material is standard and was absorbed into Berthelot–Ogus and rigid cohomology. The mixed-characteristic 'bicrystal over Spec Z' with F_p at all primes, meant to tie together formal groups in all characteristics, is a less well-known global idea that was not developed in this form. It is a modest but genuine undeveloped thread, though the Tate letter is known to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the typescript has 'Spec(W)→Spec(W)' with a handwritten 'f' inserted, i.e. 'Specf(W)' = Spf(W); the transcription's 'Spf(W)' is a fair normalisation.
'X x_R(R,f_R)' should read X ×_R (R, f_R), the base change of X by the Frobenius of R.
'Bien que f_X et par suite f_{X_K} soit loin d'être unique': 'soit' is struck out in the typescript, so the verb is missing in the original.
